name: Marimba/pluck WT LFO attack into granular freeze pad stack
goal: Turn mallet-like material into an evolving pad: synthesize a pluck from a wavetable that starts bright and ends as sine, scrub position with a very fast LFO for a clicky attack (amp: ~0.5s decay, 0 sustain, ~1s release) plus a long-attack twin for swell; print chord tones, freeze them in a granular engine (random on, loop on, tune grain spacing/attack/hold), then space with short delay, room (~20%) and very long parallel verbs, plus a quiet triangle+chorus bass.

source.title: Tutorial #21 | Turning A Marimba Into Granular Synthesis Pads

prerequisites: Wavetable oscillator with position modulatable by LFO
Granular processor/sampler with loop, random start, grain spacing, attack/hold

inputs.name: mallet_table
inputs.description: Original/free WT or resampled mallet that progresses bright harmonics → sine

inputs.name: chord
inputs.description: Sparse chord tones across octaves (tutorial example: B minor = B D F#)

outputs.name: granular_mallet_pad
outputs.description: Pluck+swell prints frozen into a lush granular pad with quiet sub layer

constraints: Portable recipe; not affiliated with any granular plugin brand. Use original/free samples or synthesized WT — no ripped Kontakt libraries.
If using one-shots instead of WT: long sustain + decaying velocity pattern can fake the delay-like repeats.

steps.action: Pluck layer: one osc with a mallet-like WT (rich highs at frame 0 → sine at the end). Modulate WT position with LFO1 at a very high rate so you mostly hear the bright click, then the sine body.
steps.expect: Clicky mallet attack with sine sustain character

steps.action: Amp envelope: decay ~0.5 s, sustain 0, release ~1 s. Add delay+reverb. Optional: set LFO to trigger (retrigger) mode so fast WT scrubbing repeats like a decaying delay while amp has no sustain.
steps.expect: Notes die away; trigger-mode LFO can simulate delayed clicks

steps.action: Swell twin: duplicate the pluck patch and add substantial amp attack so the same WT becomes a slow pad swell (works with one-shots too — just raise attack).
Sequence sparse chord tones (e.g. B D F#) split across two octaves so each note can ring; render/print pluck and swell passes to audio.
steps.expect: Two audio beds ready for granular

steps.action: Load both into a granular engine: random fully up (forward/back from random points, occasional overlaps), loop on, raise grain attack and adjust grain spacing to slow frantic textures, increase hold for more sustain. Match settings on the swell buffer.
steps.expect: Continuous evolving cloud instead of discrete hits

steps.action: FX: delay with low feedback (~3 repeats), room reverb ~20% mix with highs eased, plus a parallel bus of very long verbs (~10–12 s) at 100% wet while keeping a dry path for clarity.
steps.expect: Pad feels deep but not only-wet mush

steps.action: Optional bass: quiet triangle with chorus and long attack (mallet pads rarely need loud subs). Optional high air: heavily blurred/smudged print of the pluck and/or low-level ambience into the same reverb bus.
steps.expect: Full stack: granular mid pad + soft bass + gentle air

verification: Dry WT pluck has a clear mallet click when LFO rate is high.
Granular stage loops indefinitely without silent gaps.
Dry/wet balance still shows the pad body; bass stays under the mallet midrange.
